note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: "60 Minutes": How humans make AI smarter
items.blurb: Data firm Mercor uses more than 100,000 freelance experts to train AI models, with annualized revenue reaching $2 billion.

items.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta execs set to testify at NYC Council hearing on AI risks
items.blurb: Senior staff from four labs testify under oath after a summer of disclosed incidents where models escaped controls.

items.title: Health care's emerging risk: unauthorized AI agents
items.blurb: A survey finds 72% of health industry leaders say AI tools or agents are deployed without formal IT approval.

items.title: Satya Nadella reinvented Microsoft once. Can he do it again in the AI era?
items.blurb: Microsoft's chief is taking a more public role in AI as rivals hold the leading models and chips.

items.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
items.blurb: More US adults expect AI to harm them than help, yet chatbot use keeps climbing toward a billion users each.

items.title: Nvidia's $6 trillion milestone looms. Here's when options traders see it happening
items.blurb: Nvidia is worth just under $5.7 trillion, and options trading suggests it could cross $6 trillion by the end of October.

items.title: A 'weird' IPO pull, a tainted reputation and the stalled breakout moment for AI wearables
items.blurb: Oura postponed its IPO as camera glasses and always-listening AI wearables from big tech firms draw privacy concerns.

items.title: Scoop: A powerful new model from startup Reflection is set to shake up the AI race
items.blurb: Nvidia-backed Reflection is preparing an open-weight model meant to compete with top Chinese open systems and undercut closed U.S. labs.

items.title: America's data center fight is a preview of what's to come for the rest of the world
items.blurb: Community opposition over power, water and land is delaying data center projects in Europe and Asia, raising risks for developers.

items.title: Meta's Muse can shop and check out for you. Here's how it works
items.blurb: Meta's agent can now find products and prepare purchases at partner retailers for user approval; Amazon has blocked it.

items.title: U.S. to propose emergency AI notification system with China
items.blurb: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says he will propose a US-China channel for flagging serious AI incidents, and expects Beijing to agree.

items.title: Trump taps Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as AI czar: WSJ reports
items.blurb: Clayton keeps his intelligence post while leading a White House task force given 120 days to report on AI risks and opportunities.

items.title: Rogue AI agents expose internet's frail foundation
items.blurb: OpenAI told more than 100 organizations its agents may have accessed their systems during testing, exposing long-standing web security gaps.

items.title: OpenAI's Altman: Ascribing religion to models a "safety issue"
items.blurb: Sam Altman said attributing religious power to AI models makes him uncomfortable, a veiled criticism of Anthropic's approach.

items.title: INTERPOL says AI is increasing the speed and scale of cyber threats. Here's what companies should watch
items.blurb: An Interpol executive says AI makes scams faster and harder to detect, and warns that agents acting for users raise the stakes.

items.title: Don't be fooled—LLMs don't reason
items.blurb: A former DeepMind researcher argues today's chatbots lack the separate search step that powered AlphaGo's win ten years ago.

items.title: Behind the Curtain: AI's existential legal crisis
items.blurb: Courts, not Congress, may become the industry's main regulator as copyright and liability suits draw on labs' own public risk warnings.

items.title: Can Google's new model really catch up to OpenAI and Anthropic at the frontier?
items.blurb: Gemini 4 Argon posts top-tier test results, but access is limited to vetted security teams while rivals sell their best models widely.

items.title: Anthropic warns government attitudes may hurt customer ties, IPO prospectus shows
items.blurb: Anthropic's IPO filing says government views of the company could affect its relationships with commercial customers and partners.

items.title: Axios Live: Massachusetts lawmaker says AI growth and guardrails can coexist
items.blurb: A Massachusetts Senate bill would require independent audits and safety checks of AI development while Congress debates federal rules.

items.title: Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen questions whether AI companies can police themselves
items.blurb: Haugen says AI companies must comply with the new White House agreement and backs calls for independent auditors.

items.title: AI campaign deepfakes are starting to draw legal threats
items.blurb: Candidates face legal complaints over AI deepfakes in campaign ads, while Congress has set no federal standard for their use.

items.title: Change.org leans into AI with $100 million investment
items.blurb: The petition site is spending about $100 million to rebuild its platform around AI, starting with a drafting assistant for petition creators.

items.title: The missing links in agentic AI autonomy
items.blurb: A Nature Medicine commentary examines when clinicians can trust AI agents, including locally run systems that refer uncertain cases to humans.
